name: Drug- or toxin-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension
aliases: PAH induced by drugs or toxins

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) Pulmonary Hypertension Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest confirmed by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
History of exposure to known causative drugs or toxins (e.g., anorexigens, methamphetamines, chemotherapeutic agents)
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as connective tissue disease, congenital heart disease, or chronic thromboembolic disease
Echocardiographic evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy or dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hemodynamic confirmation by right heart catheterization with mPAP ≥ 25 mmHg and PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg, documented exposure to causative drug or toxin, and exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful history taking to identify drug or toxin exposure and exclusion of other etiologies.

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or N-terminal proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery pressures
Chest X-ray demonstrating enlarged pulmonary arteries and right heart enlargement
High-resolution CT to exclude parenchymal lung disease
other: Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure and normal wedge pressure
History of exposure to causative drugs or toxins (e.g., fenfluramine, methamphetamine, dasatinib)

distinguishingFeatures: No history of drug or toxin exposure
Similar hemodynamic profile but idiopathic etiology
History or evidence of chronic pulmonary embolism
Ventilation-perfusion scan showing mismatched perfusion defects
Different treatment approach including possible surgical intervention

redFlags: Rapid progression of dyspnea and right heart failure symptoms
Syncope episodes indicating severe hemodynamic compromise
Signs of right ventricular failure such as marked peripheral edema and ascites
